fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Nighttime conspicuity of a HAWK/PHB display amid background clutter is a recognized, scheme-relevant safety issue at an arterial pedestrian crossing, squarely within final-design-stage RSA scope.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal driver-confusion claim rests on a verbatim quote from EV-US-001 ('Drivers may be confused by competing background visual elements at night') tied to a site-specific case study record, exceeding registry-citation-only.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed purely as a safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics with no compliance assertion or normative-basis conflation, keeping safety and regulatory questions categorically distinct.
justifications.recommendation_quality: A reflective border around the signal head is a specific, actionable, and implementable countermeasure at final design, directly targeting the identified conspicuity deficiency at the named intersection.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians—the exposed users if drivers detect or interpret the beacon late—are explicitly identified and linked to the driver-conspicuity mechanism, so VRU impact is both applicable and addressed.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance adequacy for slower walkers at signalized/HAWK crossings on the corridor's highest ped-bike collision sites is a genuine final-design-stage safety matter with direct crash-exposure relevance.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim ('clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') is backed by a verbatim quote under cited evidence_id EV-US-016 tied to the recorded case-study issue for these sites; no invented content detected.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed as a categorical safety_concern to verify design walking-speed assumptions under FHWA/MUTCD semantics, not conflated with any compliance/code-violation assertion.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable (reprogramme clearance intervals across all six HAWK sites at a reduced assumed walking speed); citing a concrete speed value (e.g., MUTCD lower-walking-speed provision) would strengthen it further.
justifications.vru_coverage: Elderly pedestrians are explicitly identified as the affected road users and are the core focus of the finding, fully addressing VRU impact.
